content: 1. Comprehensive contraceptive information and services must be provided, including emergency, short-acting, and long-acting contraceptive methods. 2. All individuals and communities should have access to the health services they require without experiencing financial hardship or discrimination. 3. Evidence-based, comprehensive sexuality education (CSE) must be made available to everyone in accessible formats and languages. 4. Accurate, unbiased, and evidence-based information on sexual and reproductive health (SRH), including abortion and contraceptive methods, must be widely accessible in multiple formats and languages. 5. Health systems must be adequately resourced, ensuring the availability, accessibility, affordability, and quality of essential medicines, supplies, equipment, workforce, and financial allocations. 6. Equitable access to quality-assured essential medicines and health products must be guaranteed. 7. Leadership and clinical standards should promote evidence-based SRH services. 8. Health systems must respect SRH and human rights, including non-discrimination, equality, and autonomy in decision-making. 9. The healthcare workforce must be robust, receive competency-based training, and be skilled in providing evidence-based SRH counseling and services. 10. SRH services must be delivered by individuals trained in the legal and policy frameworks, ensuring rights-compliant practices. 11. Confidentiality and privacy in care must be ensured, with efforts to counteract abortion stigma. 12. Safe and timely access to comprehensive abortion care must be available, preventing the need for unsafe abortions. 13. Health financing policies should avoid making access to SRH services conditional on direct payments at the point of service. 14. Care must always be provided respectfully and compassionately. 15. Communities should be engaged and supportive in the provision of SRH services. 16. Human rights must be respected, protected, and fulfilled, requiring regular review and revision of laws and policies to align with evolving international human rights standards. 17. States must take measures to prevent unsafe abortions and reduce maternal mortality and morbidity, addressing the physical and mental risks associated with unsafe abortion. 18. States are obligated to liberalize restrictive abortion laws, ensure access to quality abortion and post-abortion care, and respect women's autonomy in making decisions about their SRH. 19. States must ensure that the regulation of abortion does not force individuals to resort to unsafe abortions or jeopardize their lives, subject them to physical or mental suffering, discriminate against them, or interfere arbitrarily with their privacy. 20. Abortion regulations must be evidence-based and proportionate, ensuring respect for human rights. 21. States must ensure that SRH facilities, goods, and services are available, accessible, acceptable, and of good quality. 22. Accurate healthcare information, including on abortion, must be provided without fear of criminal sanctions. 23. SRH services must be delivered in a culturally respectful and sensitive manner, considering gender, age, disability, sexual diversity, and life-cycle requirements. 24. States must ensure equal access to the same range, quality, and standard of SRH information, goods, and services for all individuals. 25. Particular attention must be given to marginalized groups, those with limited resources, rural populations, and minorities, ensuring their access to safe abortion and post-abortion care. 26. Discriminatory laws, policies, and practices that impair access to SRH, such as criminalization of abortion and restrictive abortion laws, must be repealed or reformed. 27. States must prevent forced abortions, particularly among marginalized groups, and ensure that all abortions are conducted with the free and informed consent of the individual. 28. States must provide effective and confidential access to safe, legal abortion in cases where the life or health of the pregnant individual is at risk, where the pregnancy results from rape or incest, or where the pregnancy is non-viable. 29. States must take steps to reduce maternal morbidity and mortality, addressing unsafe abortion and ensuring timely healthcare access. 30. SRH services, including abortion and post-abortion care, must respect the privacy and confidentiality of individuals. 31. Healthcare professionals must not be mandated to report cases of individuals who have undergone abortions. 32. Denial of therapeutic abortion may constitute an arbitrary interference with the right to privacy. 33. Third-party authorization requirements for abortion may violate the right to privacy. 34. Forced abortion, criminalization of abortion, denial or delay of safe abortion care, and mistreatment of individuals seeking SRH services are forms of gender-based violence and may amount to torture or cruel, inhuman, or degrading treatment. 35. States must ensure that abortion regulations do not subject individuals to substantial physical or mental suffering, such as in cases of rape. 36. States must prevent and prosecute forced abortions conducted by public officials or private actors, including in the context of coercive family planning laws or conflict. 37. Individuals seeking safe, legal abortion must not be subjected to humiliating or judgmental attitudes that delay or deny services, especially in contexts of extreme vulnerability. 38. Criminalization of abortion may amount to torture or cruel, inhuman, or degrading treatment, including practices such as extracting confessions for prosecution purposes from individuals seeking emergency medical care due to illegal abortion. 39. States must ensure access to family planning and SRH information and services, including affordable contraceptive methods, enabling individuals to make autonomous and informed decisions about their reproductive health. 40. Women with disabilities must be able to exercise their right to decide on the number and spacing of their children. 41. States must ensure that up-to-date, accurate SRH information is publicly available and accessible to all individuals in appropriate languages and formats. 42. Educational institutions must incorporate unbiased, scientifically accurate, evidence-based, age-appropriate, and comprehensive sexuality education into their required curricula. 43. Accurate, evidence-based abortion information must be made available to individuals on a confidential basis. 44. Informed consent must be provided freely, safeguarded effectively, and based on complete, high-quality, accurate, and accessible information. 45. States must ensure adequate access to essential medicines in an affordable manner. 46. States must ensure access to necessary, up-to-date scientific technologies, particularly contraception and medicines for abortion, without discrimination. 47. Access to abortion must be available when carrying a pregnancy to term would cause substantial pain or suffering, including situations where the life or health of the individual is at risk, the pregnancy results from rape or incest, or the pregnancy is non-viable.
